newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $12.29 billion.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $12.29 billion.

text.p: Venezuela's foreign reserves rose $195 million, or 1.6 percent, to $12.288 billion in the week to Sept 6, according to figures released by the central bank.

Reserves were up from a revised $12.093 bln on August 30, the bank's latest weekly bulletin of indicators showed, and up $2.586 billion from reserve levels of $9.702 billion on April 19 -- the last working day before exchange levels were lifted on April 22.
From the start of the year, reserve levels were up $2.565 billion, or 26 percent.
Government officials had targeted foreign reserves to grow by $1.5 billion over the course of 1996 as part of Venezuela's IMF-supported economic adjustment program.
Venezuela's foreign reserves fell $1.784 billion, or 15.5 percent, in 1995 to end the year at $9.723 billion, the figures showed.
